## 1. One-paragraph verdict
Genuine VP9-in-IVF fixture. Container and contents verified by direct binary parse: DKIF signature, version 0, header length 32, fourcc `VP90`, 640x480, rate 30 / scale 1 (30 fps), header frame count 90, and the frame table contains exactly 90 frames with zero trailing bytes. Frame payloads range 3,944–17,367 bytes (first/key frame 16,768 bytes) and the first payload byte 0x82 carries the mandatory VP9 frame_marker `10b` — a structurally valid VP9 uncompressed-header start. The fixture is consumed by a real differential test (`vp9_differential.rs`) asserting per-frame identity plus a whole-stream MD5 against a pinned ffmpeg libvpx-vp9 constant, and that test passed in the orchestrator baseline.

## 2. What actually works (verified)
— verified by `python3` IVF parse -> `parsed frames: 90 trailing bytes: 0`, `w 640 h 480 rate 30 scale 1 nframes 90`, `first size 16768 max 17367 min 3944`, `frame1 byte 0x82 frame_marker=2`.
— verified by `rg -n vp9 audit/runs/baseline/cargo-test-workspace.txt` -> line 1390 `test differential_lanes_vs_ffmpeg_libvpx_vp9 ... ok` (4 passed, 0 failed in that binary, baseline file audit/runs/baseline/cargo-test-workspace.txt:1384-1394).

## 3. Findings
None. Checked: header field sanity (version 0, hdrlen 32), declared-vs-actual frame count equality (90 == 90), no truncated final frame, no trailing garbage, fourcc matches test's decoder lane, timestamps monotonically non-decreasing and not all zero (variable — real encode stamps), frame sizes consistent with a real keyframe+interframe encode (not 90 identical buffers).
